newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan EPA report paints mixed picture of economy.
newsitem.headline: Japan EPA report paints mixed picture of economy.

text.p: Japan's economy, despite a temporary slowdown, is continuing to recover, led by firm private demand, the Economic Planning Agency (EPA) said in its latest monthly report on Friday.
"Although the tempo of the recovery has temporarily slowed down, the economy is continuing to recover centring around firm private demand," the report said.

The closely watched wording of the monthly economic assessment changed for the first time since November 1996, dropping the word "gradual" in its description of the basic trend of recovery in the economy.
An EPA official said the "undercurrent" or basic trend of the economy could no longer be described as "gradual" as the recovery was now centring around private demand.
The official also said that, although the agency's assessment of the economy had not strengthened, it's view of the economy was now a little brighter.
Until last month, the ministry maintained a view that Japan's economy was continuing to improve and private demand was firm, although the pace of the recovery was gradual.
A rising trend in production and an improvement in employment conditions were supporting the recovery, he said.
But the official said that the present state of the economic recovery, in contrast to the basic trend, was seeing the negative effects of a tax rise in April and remained "gradual".
A fall in private consumption was the most notable effect of the rise in the national consumption tax to five percent from three percent on April 1, he said.
He said the ministry was still in the process of judging the effects of the tax rise.
"It's still too early to become optimistic or pessimistic over the outcome of the tax rise," he said.
The report also said Japan's surplus in the trade of goods and services was rising and this was contributing to the economic recovery.
The official added that Tokyo's exports were likely to remain on a rising trend, although not at as fast a pace as has been seen recently.
"The trend (of strong exports) is unlikely to change, taking into account the lingering effect of the weak yen (from earlier this year)," he said.
